arguments.value: Synchron, a California corporation with its principal place of business in San Diego, and Rare Element Resources Ltd., a British Columbia corporation with its principal place of business in Littleton, Colorado, entered into an intellectual property rights agreement tied to a separate investment agreement and option. The company granted Synchron a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive, irrevocable license during the option period to use its rare earth mineral processing and separation patents and related technical information, including the right to make improvements and, through affiliates, sublicense. If the option is not exercised before the option period ends, the license continues on a non-exclusive basis for an annual fee, but Synchron cannot sublicense to third parties. If the option is exercised before the end of the option period, the license becomes exclusive, perpetual, fully paid-up, and sublicensable to third parties. The company keeps a limited non-exclusive right for itself and its affiliates, and Synchron must keep unpublished technical information confidential except in limited circumstances. The company controls patent prosecution but must let Synchron step in if it plans to abandon patent rights. Improvements made by the company become part of the licensed technology; improvements made by Synchron belong to Synchron, with the company getting a limited license back; jointly made improvements also belong to Synchron, with a limited license back to the company. The company disclaims warranties about the technical information, but represents the covered methods and products should not infringe third-party rights and must indemnify Synchron for losses from any breach of that representation. The agreement lasts from the effective date until the last-to-expire patent expires, and certain rights can survive longer where patents remain enforceable. The governing law is the substantive law of New York and the United States of America, with disputes handled first by negotiation, then mediation, and then litigation in a court of competent jurisdiction under the Investment Agreement's jurisdiction rules.
